findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After a caller invokes the function returned by `attach`, the handler remains registered. Subsequent messages still reach disposed consumers, while repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate handlers and duplicate processing.

findings.title: [P1] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body: Calling the function returned by `startPolling` no longer stops its interval. Polling therefore continues after disposal, repeated cycles accumulate recurring work, and the live timer may prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, subsequent `"message"` events still call the handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate handlers, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation when polling stops
findings.body:
Invoking the returned stop function no longer clears the interval, so `refresh` continues every second after cancellation. Repeated start/stop cycles stack background work, and the live timer can prevent Node.js processes from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the function returned by `attach` no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any consumer that disposes an attachment will continue receiving messages, causing duplicate processing and retained handlers after reattachment.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body:
Calling the function returned by `startPolling` no longer stops polling. Once started, `refresh` runs every second indefinitely after disposal; in Node.js the live interval can also prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, calling the returned disposer no longer revokes the handler. Subsequent untrusted messages still execute code belonging to the disposed session; if the socket is reassigned, this can expose new-session data to stale handlers or perform actions under stale authorization context.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body:
Every `startPolling` call creates a permanent interval whose handle is discarded. Calling the returned cleanup cannot stop callbacks; in Node.js the interval also keeps the process alive indefinitely, while repeated start/cleanup cycles accumulate recurring CPU and I/O work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
When the returned disposer is called while the socket remains alive, it leaves `handler` registered and retained. Repeated attach/dispose cycles therefore accumulate listeners, memory, and duplicate message-processing work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
